title: Pricing mobility services under decision-dependent demand uncertainty: a carsharing case
summary: The problem of pricing mobility services has attracted significant attention. In most studies, uncertain demand is modeled as an exogenous random variable with known distribution. This assumption overlooks the likely effect of prices on user adoption decisions. To address this dependency, we formulate the pricing problem as a stochastic program with decision-dependent demand uncertainty. Specifically, we make the non-standard assumption that the probability distribution of demand depends on pricing decisions.
